newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen firm on storm - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen firm on storm - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Tuesday were seen selling steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, supported by light hog receipts amid possible transportation disruptions by a winter storm moving into the western Corn Belt, livestock dealers said.
Up to eight inches of snow were expected overnight Monday by forecasters in southeast South Dakota, the western half of Iowa and southern Minnesota, dealers in those areas said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa and southern Minnesota could range from $54.00 to $55.00 and Illinois top prices at plants could range from $54.00-$54.50.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range $53.50 to $54.50.
Prices were underpinned by lighter-than-expected interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog marketings and projections for light receipts on Tuesday, the dealers said.
The light receipts offset thin packer buying interest, they said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog marketings Friday were 92,000 head, below the estimate of 105,000 and Saturday's receipts were 13,000, compared with 20,000, USDA said. Monday's estimate was 95,000 head, USDA said.
